meta.title: Bas Bravo — Product designer and developer
meta.description: I'm Bas Bravo, a product designer and developer with over twenty years on the web. Founder of Basezero, an independent AI-first studio. My background, how I work and where to find me.

About.title: Bas Bravo
About.lead: Product designer and developer. I've been building for the web since 2005, and today I do it with AI as part of the craft.
About.portraitAlt: Portrait of Bas Bravo, wearing glasses and a grey sweater, against a blue-grey background.
intro: I started in web design and development in 2005 and haven't stopped since. I'm a creative at heart who tries not to get lost in all the code: I enjoy deciding how a product looks and feels as much as writing what makes it work.

Today I work with founders and teams through Basezero, my independent AI-first studio. I take responsibility for the whole journey, from understanding the problem to launching something real and keeping it improving with what we learn.

items.title: Define
items.body: Understand the challenge, the people who live it and the real constraints, to decide what deserves to be built and what doesn't.

items.title: Design
items.body: Give the product its shape: scope, experience and visual identity, with explicit priorities and no noise.

items.title: Build
items.body: Develop the whole product, from interface to server, in short cycles of design, code and testing.

items.title: Launch and evolve
items.body: Put a first version in the hands of real people and grow it with judgment, adding no complexity before it's needed.

path.title: Background
path.intro: Twenty years is enough to go through several technologies, several ways of working and a few useful mistakes. Here is the short version.

items.title: From Flash to the real web
items.body: I left my programming vocational training determined never to go back to enterprise apps, and became a Flash and ActionScript devotee, working for agencies such as Acuarel and VisualPublinet. Those sites are gone, but they taught me to care about detail.

items.title: Freelance and coworking
items.body: With PHP, HTML, CSS and JavaScript I worked independently from the EspacioNido coworking, where I built a small team. I collaborated with studios like NiceMondays on projects for Plan International, Cisco and Puig, and created Builder, a headless CMS ahead of its time that taught me more than any course.

items.title: Prensa Ibérica, Faro de Vigo
items.body: At the EPI publishing group I built an online store in Prestashop integrated with internal systems, a corporate CMS in Laravel that centralises content, landing pages and tools, and the design and layout of books, events and a mobile app.

items.title: Pleg, Paradigma Digital
items.body: I led the development of web applications with Vue, Nuxt and Node: data modelling, design, backend and frontend. Among them, the labelling application for the Rioja Regulatory Council, a Paradigma success story, and a Nuxt archetype for scaling CMSs quickly and maintainably.

items.title: Basezero
items.body: My independent AI-first studio. I define, design and build products of my own and for clients, with AI driving the core of the work and experience providing the judgment.

how.title: How I work
how.quote: AI gives me speed. Experience tells me where to point it.

items.title: I take initiative and finish what I start
items.body: However hard it gets, I commit to taking every project to its goals.

items.title: I work in teams, remotely too
items.body: I care about the working atmosphere and communication so the people beside me, even virtually, keep moving with energy.

items.title: I share what I learn
items.body: If others can learn from what I do and how I do it, even better. That's why I write articles.

items.title: I listen before deciding
items.body: I assume others do many things better than I do. It's how I learn from anyone.

intro.title:
From an idea
to a real digital product.
intro.body: I work directly with founders and teams through an AI-first practice: AI guides strategy, design and development so ideas become real digital products faster, from definition through launch.

about.title: An independent, AI-first studio.
about.paragraphOne: I’m Bas Bravo, a product designer and developer. Basezero is my independent, AI-first studio: I work directly with you and own the complete journey, from understanding the problem and defining the strategy through design, development and the launch of a real solution.
about.paragraphTwo: AI guides the core of my work. It is not an add-on: I use it to explore more directions, shape the product, write code, test and learn at a pace that was not possible before. My experience provides the judgment to decide what to build, what to leave out and how to turn that speed into a solid foundation.
about.paragraphThree: I work in short, open cycles instead of imposing a fixed definition or rigid management model from the start. Each version incorporates what we learn, allowing the software to grow organically and fluidly. This method works best with founders and teams who take part in decisions and want to put a useful product in front of real people early.

articles.title: Articles
articles.body: Decisions, methods and lessons on turning an idea into a useful product without adding unnecessary complexity.

farewell.title: Let’s talk about what you want to build.
farewell.body: Tell me what you want to achieve, where the project stands and whether you have a target date. I’ll reply personally so we can decide if we are a good fit.

understand.title: Define the challenge
understand.body: Together we define the objective, context, users and constraints. AI helps us explore scenarios and turn uncertainty into a shared framework for product decisions.

shape.title: Design the direction
shape.body: We model different product directions and together convert the framework into a concrete proposal: scope, architecture, experience and visual identity, with explicit priorities.

launch.title: Build the product
launch.body: I build the product’s core through an AI-first approach, linking fast cycles of design, code and testing until a functional, integrated first version is deployed.

learn.title: Validate with evidence
learn.body: We validate the solution with the business and its users transforming what we learn into concrete decisions and priorities for the next iteration.

grow.title: Evolve with purpose
grow.body: The software evolves organically: AI lets us shape each next step around what we learn, without relying on rigid planning or adding complexity before it is needed.

lock.title: Key and lock
keys: The shear line: where every pin has to rest
lock.caption: Five pins, five hypotheses: problem, person, proposal, behaviour and viability. Cutting all four keys cost about the same; only the lock says which one fits. Here the one that turns is the third.
lock.aria: A five-pin lock with a tray of four keys. Press a key to try it, use the arrow keys to change key, space to put it in or take it out and Escape to withdraw it.
lock.spoken: Key {key}: {count} of {total} pins on the shear line; {result}.

tunnel.title: Wind tunnel
keys: The threshold we set beforehand: 25 N
Where the threshold goes up to
tunnel.caption: A wing with a 20 cm chord in a tunnel at 30 m/s. You don't need to build the aircraft to know whether the section can carry its weight: you measure one thing against a threshold set beforehand. Past about 15° the flow separates and the lift falls.
tunnel.aria: A wind tunnel with a wing section on a balance. Change the angle with the pointer, the arrow keys or by dragging; the gauge reads the lift and a lamp lights when it passes the threshold.
tunnel.spoken: Angle {alpha} degrees, lift {lift} newtons, threshold {threshold} newtons: {status}.
